newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-TAYLOR FAILS AGAIN BUT BLEWETT HITS 121.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAYLOR FAILS AGAIN BUT BLEWETT HITS 121.

text.p: Australia's captain Mark Taylor suffered another batting failure on Saturday but Greg Blewett hit a timely century ahead of the first Ashes test.
Taylor, whose place is in jeopardy after a sequence of low scores, made only five on the opening day of the three-day match against Derbyshire.
Blewett's superb 121 spurred the touring side to 362 for six declared and Derbyshire were 68 for one at the close.

Taylor was given every encouragement to play his first long innings of the tour, with Derbyshire missing the injured Dominic Cork and fellow paceman Devon Malcolm, who was a late withdrawal at the request of England's selectors.
But Taylor lasted just five overs before his growing indecision saw him unwisely choose to pull a short ball from Phillip DeFreitas outside off stump and he was caught by Paul Aldred at mid-wicket.
Justin Langer, who hit an unbeaten 152 against Gloucestershire earlier this week, was trapped lbw for one by DeFreitas two overs later, making Australia 16 for two.
However, they were the only batsmen to struggle, with Blewett seizing on the opportunity to impress before the start of the Ashes series at Edgbaston next Thursday.

Blewett added 131 with Matthew Elliott for the third wicket before the tall Victorian left-hander, a virtual certainty to open in the first test, cut Kevin Dean straight to Chris Adams at slip, having hit nine fours in his 67.
Blewett reached his half-century off 92 balls, then raced to his 100 off a further 49 as he put on 99 off 103 deliveries with Steve Waugh.
Waugh was out, having hit seven fours in his 43, when DeFreitas took a fine running catch at the cover boundary off young spinner Ian Blackwell, who was making his first-class debut.
Blewett's innings ended five overs later when paceman Andrew Harris induced him to play on with his slower ball. He hit 19 fours and two sixes.
Michael Bevan also got in some useful batting practice with 56 off 64 balls before DeFreitas bowled him with a delivery which kept low to finish with three for 61.
